newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sets specials at 3.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sets specials at 3.25 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Monday conducted a round of special purchase and resale agreements in the money market at 3.25 percent, dealers said.
The central bank intervened to add liquidity to the money market after the call loan or overnight lending rate was bid at the top of the central bank's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
"I guess there's just some dislocations in cash out there. It's mainly May tax period basically causing some dislocations," said a T-bill trader with one bank-owned brokerage.
The intervention had no policy implications and the Bank of Canada's key bank rate remained at 3.25 percent.
The yield on the three-month when-issued T-bill traded at 3.21 percent after the intervention, up from 3.17 percent on Friday.
